title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## GLAM-SLAM: Real-time Gaussian Large-Scale Mapping

### The Breakthrough
The paper introduces GLAM‑SLAM, a monocular SLAM system that uses Gaussian splatting for large‑scale outdoor mapping while running in real time. It separates tracking and mapping, employing a flow‑densification step and a sparse anchor‑grid that feeds localized MLPs, delivering a 15 % boost in reconstruction quality on KITTI, Oxford RobotCar and Málaga datasets. This makes high‑fidelity 3D maps feasible for robotics applications without sacrificing speed.

### The Caveats
The authors do not name concrete baseline methods, so the reported 15 % improvement cannot be independently verified.

## MAPS: Hierarchical Coordination for Unsignalized Intersections

### The Breakthrough
MAPS proposes a hierarchical deep‑RL architecture where a centralized Master agent emits a low‑dimensional "proto‑plan" embedding that guides decentralized vehicle controllers. Tested on 72 unsignalized intersection setups in HighwayEnv, the system achieves collision‑free navigation with significantly lower travel times and 94 % success when scaling from three‑ to five‑vehicle scenarios. The approach reduces the combinatorial action space typical of multi‑agent traffic coordination.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no comparison to existing baselines, leaving the claimed improvement unsubstantiated.

## AXIS: Community‑Driven Data Engine for Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
AXIS is a browser‑based teleoperation platform that crowdsources large‑scale manipulation demonstrations, automatically generating tasks, validating demos, and augmenting data. The resulting dataset of 207 tasks and over 50 K trajectories boosts continual pre‑training success rates by 5.8 % (π₀.₅) and outperforms a RoboCasa365‑pretrained model by 37.3 % on the AXIS held‑out benchmark, especially under layout and sensor noise variations.

### The Caveats
Results are limited to the AXIS benchmark with no real‑world robot experiments, so transfer to hardware is uncertain.

## VoLN: Vision-Only Long-Horizon Navigation for UAVs

### The Breakthrough
VoLN defines a vision‑only long‑horizon navigation paradigm where goal images serve as destinations and all route information is inferred online. The baseline VoLN‑MLLM aligns self‑supervised visual features to a semantic space and predicts short‑horizon waypoints, yielding the first quantitative results (7.4 %–1.8 % success) on a 7,210‑episode UAV benchmark.

### The Caveats
Only raw success rates on a simulated benchmark are reported, with no comparison to existing navigation methods.

## Cubic Doggo 06R: 12‑DOF Quadruped with IMU

### The Breakthrough
The upgraded open‑source repo adds a 6‑axis IMU for onboard state estimation and reinforces the mechanical structure while preserving the 12‑degree‑of‑freedom leg design, enabling more expressive locomotion than the original version.

### The Caveats
The robot is showcased without quantitative locomotion results or simulation benchmarks, leaving its real‑world performance unproven.

## pointcaster: Real-Time 3D Point Cloud Engine

### The Breakthrough
pointcaster is a C++ engine that captures, fuses, and streams live point‑cloud data from depth sensors (e.g., Orbbec, Azure Kinect) and broadcasts it via low‑latency OSC, MIDI, or MQTT, with plugins for Unity, Unreal Engine, and TouchDesigner for immediate integration.

### The Caveats
No performance, latency, or scalability benchmarks are provided, so real‑time suitability for robotics remains unclear.

## ROSClaw: Trustworthy Execution Runtime for Embodied Agents

### The Breakthrough
ROSClaw offers an open‑source runtime that maps high‑level LLM‑style intents to robot actions, issuing immutable execution receipts and integrating e‑URDF grounding, sandbox safety, and verified simulation pipelines in MuJoCo and Gazebo; early hardware runs show full‑cycle verification on a UR5e and single‑step loops on an RH56 arm.

### The Caveats
The system is not benchmarked against existing ROS‑based agent frameworks, leaving its claimed trustworthiness unsubstantiated.

## Synaptic Harmony: Distributed Q‑Learning Swarm Foraging

### The Breakthrough
The repository provides a Python‑only simulation where each forager maintains its own NumPy Q‑table, enabling fully distributed learning in a dynamic gridworld with renewable resources, configurable obstacles, and real‑time rendering that visualizes emergent swarm dynamics over thousands of episodes.

### The Caveats
Behavior is demonstrated only in a self‑made gridworld with no baseline comparisons, so claimed advantages are unverified.

### Priority
GLAM‑SLAM delivers a concrete, real‑time mapping improvement that can be directly tested on existing robot datasets, making it the most actionable development today.

### One action
Clone the GLAM‑SLAM repo, run the provided KITTI example, and compare its reconstruction quality on your own outdoor sequences.
